topics.definition: Linux is an open-source, Unix-like operating system kernel used in servers, desktops, mobile devices and embedded systems.
tips: Linux is free and highly customizable.

topics.definition: Linux was created by Linus Torvalds in 1991 and is developed by a global open-source community.
tips: Many distributions are built on the Linux kernel.

topics.definition: Linux architecture consists of hardware, kernel, shell and user applications.
A Linux distribution combines the Linux kernel with software and package managers.
tips: Choose a distribution based on your needs.

topics.definition: The kernel is the core of Linux and manages memory, processes, devices and files.
tips: Do not modify the kernel unless necessary.

topics.definition: The shell is the command-line interface used to interact with Linux.
tips: Bash is the most common Linux shell.

topics.definition: Linux organizes files in a hierarchical directory structure starting from the root directory (/).
Linux is secure, stable, fast and highly customizable.
Some commercial software and hardware have limited Linux support.
Keep the system updated, use strong passwords and follow the principle of least privilege.
